::: {.portfolio-section}
## How can styling improve a portfolio?

A consistent design helps visitors identify the author, scan information, and navigate between projects. This portfolio uses black body text, a burgundy navigation bar, a pastel background, and a clover-shaped portrait.

| Tool | Purpose | Example on this website |
|---|---|---|
| HTML | Structures page elements | Headings, links, and content containers |
| CSS | Controls appearance | Background gradients, card spacing, and photo mask |
| SCSS | Extends CSS with variables and other reusable features | Theme colors and a reusable example panel |

Quarto turns Markdown into HTML. Custom classes let me target specific elements without applying the same style to every paragraph.
:::

::: {.portfolio-section}
## How do I connect styling files?

The project configuration connects a base theme, an SCSS theme extension, and a CSS file:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    theme: [cosmo, custom.scss]
    css: styles.css
```

The `custom.scss` file defines theme variables. The `styles.css` file controls detailed presentation, including the background and portrait.
:::

::: {.portfolio-section}
## How does CSS change a page?

This rule adds spacing, rounded corners, and a translucent background to content panels:

```css
.portfolio-section {
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.7);
  border-radius: 20px;
  padding: 36px;
  margin-bottom: 26px;
}
```

The sections on the homepage demonstrate this class. The background uses layered CSS gradients, while the portrait uses an SVG mask referenced from CSS to create a clover shape.

### Make the layout work on phones

```css
@media (max-width: 768px) {
  .skills-grid {
    grid-template-columns: 1fr;
  }
}
```

This changes the skill cards from three columns to a single column on smaller screens.
:::

::: {.portfolio-section}
## How does SCSS support a consistent theme?

SCSS lets me define a color once and reuse it. Quarto compiles the SCSS into CSS when rendering the website.

```scss
/*-- scss:defaults --*/
$primary: #800020;
$body-color: #000000;
$navbar-bg: #800020;
$navbar-fg: #ffffff;

/*-- scss:rules --*/
.learning-example {
  border-left: 5px solid $primary;
  padding: 1rem 1.25rem;
  background: rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.85);
}
```

::: {.learning-example}
**Live SCSS example:** This panel uses the `.learning-example` rule in `custom.scss`. Its left border reuses the burgundy `$primary` variable.
:::
:::

::: {.portfolio-section}
## How do HTML and Markdown work together?

A Quarto fenced div assigns a class to a content container:

```markdown
::: {.learning-example}
A styled explanation for my audience.
:::
```

The equivalent HTML structure is:

```html
<div class="learning-example">
  <p>A styled explanation for my audience.</p>
</div>
```

This connection between structure and styling makes the design reusable across pages.

## Design decisions

- Keep body text black for readability.
- Use white navigation labels against the burgundy bar.
- Use real headings so the content remains easy to scan.
- Include meaningful alternative text for the portrait.
- Use responsive layouts and visible keyboard focus indicators.
